questions.topic: Avoir as possession
questions.learningObjective: Use avoir for possession in a note
questions.stem: Stage one: a note states what someone has. Stage two: choose the verb.

options.text: Etre, because it links subject to object

questions.explanation: Avoir expresses possession. Etre expresses identity, and the other verbs do not express possession.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The article system of a noun phrase
questions.learningObjective: Identify the article type in a phrase
questions.stem: Which article is definite plural?

options.text: Des, because it is indefinite plural
Les, because it is definite plural

questions.explanation: Les is the definite plural article. Des is indefinite plural. Le and la are singular.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: De or du after a verb
questions.learningObjective: Explain de or du after a verb
questions.stem: Explain the use of de or du after avoir besoin.

answer.exemplar: Avoir besoin takes de, which contracts to du before a masculine singular definite article, as in besoin du temps.

questions.explanation: The verb takes de, and de contracts with le to du. Before other articles, de remains unchanged.
questions.hint: De contracts to du before le.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Forms of the partitive article
questions.learningObjective: Choose the partitive article for a masculine noun

stimulus.body: The clerk bought du papier and de la colle for the office.

questions.stem: In the passage, which partitive article is used for papier?

options.text: De la, because papier is feminine
Du, because papier is masculine singular

questions.explanation: Du is the partitive article for a masculine singular noun. De la is feminine, des is plural, and de is indefinite.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: A versus au and aux
questions.learningObjective: Choose the correct a form in a note
questions.stem: Stage one: a note mentions going to a place. Stage two: choose a, au, or aux.

options.text: A before feminine, au before masculine singular, aux before plural

questions.explanation: A contracts to au before masculine singular and aux before plural. Before feminine it stays a.
questions.hint: A contracts before masculine and plural.
